newsitem.title: UK: House of Fraser sees 40-50 mln stg charge.
newsitem.headline: House of Fraser sees 40-50 mln stg charge.

text.p: Retailer House of Fraser Plc said on Tuesday it expected to make provisions of between 40 and 50 million stg in its full-year accounts for a major reorganisation of its operations.
Finance director Richard Scott said the provision would be necessary to cover possible store closures, job cuts and the write-down of inappropriate stock lines.
"On the very prudent side at this stage it's probably going to be between 40 and 50 million...It's a very conservative figure," he said in a telephone interview.

Scott declined to give any details about which stores might be sold or closed or any estimates of redundancies. He said a medium-sized store employed around 200 staff, while head offices in London and Glasgow and the computer centre in Swindon in southern England employed 550 people in all.
British newspapers speculated at the weekend that the group would shed more than 1,000 jobs.

Scott declined to say which of its 51 stores might close as the review of the stores was not complete. "There are a number of stores in major cities and shopping centres that do particularly well," he said.
He also declined to elaborate on what cost savings the reorganisation might achieve. "They're still being quantified," he said.
But he said the impact of the review on costs would start to show through by early next year.
Scott said because of lead times in fashion merchandise the impact of revamped ranges on sales and gross margins would not come through until the second half of next year and into 1998.
He said concessions sales, which carry lower margins, had done much better than House of Fraser's "own bought" merchandise, which includes own label and branded ranges.
"We make no apology for it, we've had a failure of "own bought" ladieswear," Scott said.
He said the group hoped new fashion director Ann Gordon would address the problem.
"What we did before was had a very expensive branded merchandise and a very modest priced own label range and that did not work."
He said the concessions operating within the House of Fraser stores had scored successes with quality, classic clothing.
But the group's "own bought" ranges had done poorly because they were pitched to compete with Marks and Spencer and that had proved difficult, Scott said.
